title: Shader Energy Transfer Lab
description: Two shader balls orbit a central energy core. The user redistributes a conserved pool of 100 energy units between them using sliders and direct clicks, where energy controls emission intensity, scale, and rotation speed. Each transfer couples all three properties simultaneously, and full undo/redo history tracks every state change.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads ShaderBall.glb and ShaderBall2.glb via GLTFLoader. Place them on opposite sides of a glowing central sphere (the 'energy core'), orbiting it slowly. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,8) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: one warm DirectionalLight, one cool HemisphereLight, and a PointLight at the core that pulses gently.

Core mechanic — Energy Conservation: A global pool of exactly 100 energy units is split between Ball A and Ball B. Display current values in a HUD overlay. Energy can never be created or destroyed, only transferred.

Interactions (10-14 steps expected): (1) A horizontal slider redistributes energy between the two balls (moving left gives to A, right gives to B). (2) Clicking directly on a ball transfers 5 units from the other ball to the clicked one. (3) A 'Equalize' button sets both to 50. (4) A 'Randomize' button randomly splits the 100 units. (5) Keyboard shortcuts: ArrowLeft transfers 10 to A, ArrowRight transfers 10 to B. Each ball's energy value drives three coupled properties simultaneously: emissive intensity (0-2 range mapped from 0-100 energy), uniform scale (0.5-1.5), and orbit rotation speed (0.1-2.0 rad/s). Use MeshStandardMaterial and set emissive color to blue for ShaderBall and orange for ShaderBall2. Implement full undo/redo: every energy change pushes state onto an undo stack. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes. Display undo/redo stack depth in the HUD. Clamp all values so neither ball goes below 0 or above 100. Add smooth lerp transitions (duration 0.4s) when energy values change so scale, glow, and speed animate fluidly. Show a particle stream (simple small spheres or sprites) flowing from the losing ball to the gaining ball during each transfer, with particle count proportional to transfer amount. Render the HUD with HTML/CSS overlay showing both energy values, stack depths, and brief control instructions.
